77873.q: Which explorer do these emojis mean?
77873.e: Ice, penguins and a chequered flag show reaching the South Pole. Roald Amundsen was the first to get there, on 14 December 1911.
77873.m: Roald Amundsen was the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911.

77874.q: Which mountaineer do these pictures mean?
77874.e: A mountain, footprints and the summit show the first ascent of Mount Everest. Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first to stand on top, in 1953.
77874.m: Hillary and Tenzing were the first to climb Mount Everest, in 1953.

77875.q: Which seafarer do these emojis mean?
77875.e: A kangaroo, a ship and a map show the exploration of Australia. In 1770, James Cook mapped the east coast of Australia.
77875.m: James Cook explored the east coast of Australia in 1770.

77876.q: Which scientist do these pictures mean?
77876.e: Giant tortoises, islands and finches point to the Galápagos Islands. Charles Darwin visited them in 1835 and later developed his theory of evolution.
77876.m: Charles Darwin did research on the Galápagos Islands.

77877.q: Which Swiss adventurer do these emojis mean?
77877.e: A balloon circling the Earth shows the first non-stop balloon flight around the world. Bertrand Piccard achieved it in 1999 together with Brian Jones.
77877.m: Bertrand Piccard flew around the Earth in a balloon in 1999.

77878.q: Which invention do these pictures mean?
77878.e: A lamp with a plug in the house shows the electric light bulb. Thomas Edison made it practical for everyday use around 1880.
77878.m: Thomas Edison made the light bulb practical for everyday use.

77879.q: Which invention by Johannes Gutenberg do these emojis show?
77879.e: Books, a printing machine and letters show printing with movable type. Gutenberg invented it around 1450 in Mainz.
77879.m: Gutenberg invented printing with movable type around 1450.

77880.q: Which inventor do these pictures mean?
77880.e: A bell, and the telephone, belong to Alexander Graham Bell. He received a patent for the telephone in 1876.
77880.m: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876.

77881.q: Which invention by Carl Benz do these emojis show?
77881.e: An engine, a vehicle and fuel show the motor car. In 1886, Carl Benz built the first motor car with a petrol engine.
77881.m: Carl Benz built the first car with a petrol engine in 1886.

77882.q: Which inventors do these pictures mean?
77882.e: Two brothers and an aeroplane show the Wright brothers. In 1903 they made the first controlled powered flight.
77882.m: The Wright brothers were the first to fly a powered aeroplane, in 1903.

77883.q: Which invention by Alessandro Volta do these emojis mean?
77883.e: Electric current from a store shows the battery. Around 1800, Alessandro Volta built the first battery, the voltaic pile.
77883.m: Alessandro Volta built the first battery around 1800.

77884.q: Which Swiss invention do these pictures mean?
77884.e: Burrs from plants got stuck to a dog's fur and to trousers. This gave the Swiss George de Mestral the idea for Velcro.
77884.m: Velcro was invented by a Swiss man.

77885.q: Which invention from CERN in Geneva do these emojis show?
77885.e: The world, a computer and links show the World Wide Web. Tim Berners-Lee developed it in 1989 at CERN in Geneva.
77885.m: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN in Geneva.

77886.q: Which invention do these pictures mean?
77886.e: A magnet and the points of the compass show the compass. Its needle is magnetic and points north; it was invented in China.
77886.m: The magnetic needle of a compass points north.

77887.q: Which machine of the Industrial Revolution do these emojis show?
77887.e: Rising steam, cogs and a factory show the steam engine. From 1769, James Watt improved it greatly.
77887.m: The steam engine powered the first factories.

77888.q: Which famous industry of eastern Switzerland do these emojis show?
77888.e: Thread, flower patterns and a factory show embroidery. Around 1910, St Gallen embroidery was Switzerland's most important export.

77889.q: Which machine of the textile industry do these pictures mean?
77889.e: Yarn and machine make spinning machine. It spun yarn much faster than a person at a spinning wheel.
77889.m: The spinning machine made spinning yarn much faster.

77890.q: Which problem of the Industrial Revolution do these emojis show?
77890.e: A child in a factory with long working hours shows child labour. The Swiss Factory Act of 1877 banned factory work for children under 14.
77890.m: The Factory Act of 1877 banned child labour in Swiss factories.

77891.q: Which industry of the Industrial Revolution is meant?
77891.e: A pickaxe, black rock and a shaft show coal mining. Coal was the most important fuel for steam engines.
77891.m: Coal was the most important fuel of the Industrial Revolution.

77892.q: Which development of the Industrial Revolution do these pictures show?
77892.e: Many people moved from the countryside to the towns to work in factories. This development is called urbanisation.
77892.m: During the Industrial Revolution, towns grew a lot.

77893.q: What was the first railway running entirely in Switzerland, which these emojis point to, called?
77893.e: Train and bread lead to the Spanish Bun Railway (Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn), which ran between Zurich and Baden from 1847. It was the first line entirely on Swiss soil and is said to have brought fresh pastries from Baden, the “Spanischbrötli”, to Zurich.
77893.m: The first railway line entirely in Switzerland ran from Zurich to Baden in 1847.

77894.q: Which way of producing things by Henry Ford do these pictures show?
77894.e: Cars, machines and a constant cycle show the assembly line. Henry Ford introduced it in 1913, and cars became much cheaper.
77894.m: From 1913, Henry Ford built cars on an assembly line.

77895.e: A rocket, the Moon and the first footprint lead to Neil Armstrong. In July 1969 he became the first person to step onto the Moon.
77895.m: Neil Armstrong was the first person on the Moon.

77896.q: What was the rocket that these pictures point to called?
77896.e: Rocket, the planet Saturn and the number 5 make Saturn V. This rocket took the Apollo astronauts to the Moon.
77896.m: The Saturn V took the astronauts to the Moon.

77897.q: What was the lunar module that these emojis point to called?
77897.e: An eagle on the Moon stands for the lunar module Eagle. Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon in it in 1969.
77897.m: The lunar module of Apollo 11 was called Eagle.

77898.q: Which astronaut do these pictures mean?
77898.e: An astronaut, the number 2 and the Moon lead to Buzz Aldrin. Shortly after Armstrong, he became the second person to step onto the Moon.
77898.m: Buzz Aldrin was the second person on the Moon.

77899.q: Which Apollo 11 astronaut do these emojis mean?
77899.e: An astronaut circling the Moon in a spacecraft is Michael Collins. He stayed in the command module Columbia while the other two landed.
77899.m: Michael Collins orbited the Moon while his colleagues landed.

77900.q: Which mission do these pictures mean?
77900.e: A rocket and the number 11 show Apollo 11. On this mission in 1969, people landed on the Moon for the first time.
77900.m: Apollo 11 took the first people to the Moon in 1969.

77901.q: Which Swiss experiment on the Moon do these emojis show?
77901.e: Sun, wind and a sheet on the Moon show the solar wind sail of the University of Bern. It caught particles of the solar wind and was even set up before the US flag.
77901.m: In 1969, an experiment from the University of Bern stood on the Moon.

77902.q: Which famous sentence about the Moon landing do these pictures mean?
a: That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind
77902.e: A small step, a giant leap and the whole world make Armstrong's famous sentence. He said it as he took his first step onto the Moon.
77902.m: Armstrong spoke of a small step and a giant leap.

77903.q: Which event in Swiss history do these emojis show?
77903.e: Three men raising their hands to swear an oath in a meadow show the Rütli Oath. According to legend, men from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore on the Rütli to help each other.
77903.m: The Rütli Oath is an important legend about the founding of Switzerland.

77904.q: Which document of Swiss history do these pictures mean?
77904.e: A charter and the year 1291 show the Federal Charter. In it, Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden promised to help each other; it is kept in the Museum of the Swiss Charters of Confederation in Schwyz.
77904.m: The Federal Charter of 1291 is seen as the founding document of Switzerland.

77905.q: Which Swiss person do these emojis mean?
77905.e: A red cross, an ambulance and a prize lead to Henri Dunant. He started the founding of the Red Cross in Geneva in 1863 and in 1901 was one of the first to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
77905.m: Henri Dunant founded the Red Cross.

77906.q: Which right from Swiss history do these pictures show?
77906.e: A woman, a ballot box and a yes show women's right to vote. At national level, women in Switzerland have only been allowed to vote and elect since 1971.
77906.m: Since 1971, Swiss women have been able to vote and elect at national level.

77907.q: Which movement, led by Zwingli in Zurich, do these emojis show?
77907.e: The Bible, a church and renewal show the Reformation. Huldrych Zwingli started it in Zurich from 1519.
77907.m: Huldrych Zwingli brought the Reformation to Zurich.

77908.q: Which document from 1848 do these pictures mean?
77908.e: A legal text, the scales of justice and a government building show the Federal Constitution. With it, Switzerland became a federal state in 1848.
77908.m: Since the Federal Constitution of 1848, Switzerland has been a federal state.

77909.q: Which Swiss troop do these emojis mean?
77909.e: A guard at a church and a palace shows the Pontifical Swiss Guard. It has guarded the Pope in the Vatican since 1506.
77909.m: The Swiss Guard has protected the Pope since 1506.

77910.q: Which Swiss educator do these pictures mean?
77910.e: A teacher, a child, books and a heart lead to Pestalozzi. He worked for the education of poor children and wanted to develop “head, heart and hand”.
77910.m: Pestalozzi wanted to develop children's head, heart and hand.

77911.q: Which mountain railway, opened in 1912, do these emojis mean?
77911.e: A train, a young girl and a mountain make the Jungfrau Railway, because Jungfrau means maiden. Since 1912 it has run up to the Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe.
77911.m: The Jungfrau Railway has run up to the Jungfraujoch since 1912.

77912.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77912.e: In the evening, the street lamps were lit with fire and a ladder. That was the job of the lamplighter, before there was electric light.
77912.m: In the past, lamplighters lit the street lamps every evening.

77913.q: Which job from the past do these pictures mean?
77913.e: Wood, fire and black charcoal show the charcoal burner. He slowly charred wood in a kiln with little air and made charcoal this way.
77913.m: The charcoal burner made charcoal in a kiln.

77914.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77914.e: A basket of clothes by the water shows the washerwoman. Without washing machines, washerwomen washed clothes by hand in a stream or at a fountain.
77914.m: In the past, washerwomen washed the laundry by hand.

77915.q: Which craft is meant by these pictures?
77915.e: A barrel, wood and a hammer show the cooper. He makes barrels from wooden staves and iron hoops.

77916.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77916.e: Letters, horses, the post horn and mountains show the stagecoach driver. Before there was a railway, stagecoaches travelled, for example, over the Gotthard Pass.
77916.m: Stagecoach drivers blew the post horn and carried post and travellers over the passes.

77917.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77917.e: Grain, a mill wheel and water show the miller. In the watermill, he grinds grain into flour.
77917.m: The miller grinds grain into flour.

77918.q: Which job from the past do these emojis mean?
77918.e: A horn, the night and a village show the night watchman. He walked through the lanes at night, called out the hours and sounded the alarm if there was a fire.
77918.m: The night watchman called out the hours at night.

77919.q: Which craft is meant by these pictures?
77919.e: Knotted cords and twisting show the rope maker. He twisted fibres from hemp into cords and ropes.
77919.m: The rope maker twists fibres into ropes.

77920.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77920.e: A woman at a computer who fixes errors in the program (“bugs”) is a computer scientist. She develops and repairs software.
77920.m: Computer scientists develop programs for computers.

77921.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77921.e: A building, a set square and a house show the architect. She plans and designs buildings.
77921.m: An architect plans and designs buildings.

77922.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77922.e: Hair, scissors and a mirror show the hairdresser. She cuts, colours and styles hair.
77922.m: A hairdresser cuts and styles hair.

77923.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77923.e: A gateau, a slice of cake and a cupcake show the pastry chef. She bakes and decorates gateaux and fine cakes.
77923.m: A pastry chef makes gateaux and cakes.

77924.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77924.e: A test tube, a microscope and a lab coat show the lab technician. She carries out experiments and measurements in the laboratory.
77924.m: Lab technicians work with microscopes and test tubes.

77925.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77925.e: Medicines, a prescription and a shop show the pharmacist. She hands out medicines and gives advice on how to take them.
77925.m: In the chemist's, pharmacists give advice about medicines.

77926.q: Which job do these emojis mean?
77926.e: Trees, a saw and a worker with a helmet show the forester. He looks after the forest and cuts down trees.
77926.m: A forester looks after the forest.

77927.q: Which job do these pictures mean?
77927.e: A newspaper, a microphone and a camera show the journalist. She researches and reports on news.
77927.m: Journalists research and report on news.

77928.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77928.e: Volleyball and beach make beach volleyball. It is played in pairs on sand.
77928.m: In beach volleyball, two play against two on sand.

77929.q: Which team sport do these pictures show?
77929.e: Water, swimming and a ball stand for water polo. Two teams swim and throw a ball into the other team's goal.
77929.m: In water polo, you throw the ball into the goal while swimming.

77930.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77930.e: Running in the forest with a map and compass is orienteering. You try to find checkpoints in the terrain as fast as possible.
77930.m: In orienteering, you find the checkpoints with a map and compass.

77931.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77931.e: A sailing boat, wind and the chequered flag show sailing. The Swiss team Alinghi won the America's Cup in 2003.
77931.m: In sailing, the wind drives the boat.

77932.q: Which Swiss sport do these pictures show?
77932.e: Two fighters in sawdust from wood and a bull as a prize go with Schwingen, Swiss wrestling. The winner at the Federal Wrestling Festival often gets a bull.
77932.m: In Schwingen, two wrestlers fight in a ring of sawdust.

77933.q: Which sport do these pictures show?
77933.e: A flag in the hole and a player with a club show golf. The aim is to get the ball into the hole with as few strokes as possible.
77933.m: In golf, you need as few strokes as possible to reach the hole.

77934.q: Which competition do these pictures mean?
77934.e: A rider at a gallop and the chequered flag make a horse race. In St Moritz, horse races even take place on the frozen lake.
77934.m: In a horse race, the fastest horse wins.

77935.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77935.e: Art (paint palette) and gymnastics make artistic gymnastics. You do exercises on apparatus such as the high bar, parallel bars and floor.
77935.m: In artistic gymnastics, you perform on different pieces of apparatus.

77936.q: Which sport do these pictures mean?
77936.e: Mountain and bike make mountain bike. You ride a mountain bike off-road and in the mountains.
77936.m: With a mountain bike you can ride over rough ground.

77937.q: Which Olympic custom do these pictures mean?
77937.e: Fire and a runner make the torch relay. The Olympic flame is lit in Olympia in Greece and carried to the host city.
77937.m: The Olympic flame is lit in Olympia.

77938.q: Which symbol do these pictures mean?
77938.e: Five rings are the symbol of the Olympic Games. They stand for the five continents that come together at the Games.
77938.m: The five Olympic rings stand for the five continents.

77939.q: Which prize for winners at the ancient Olympic Games do these pictures show?
77939.e: A Greek temple, olives and a crown show the olive wreath. In ancient Olympia, the winners received a wreath made from branches of the olive tree.
77939.m: In ancient times, Olympic winners received an olive wreath.

77940.q: Which major event do these pictures mean?
77940.e: Snow, mountains and a medal go with the Winter Olympics. In Switzerland, they took place in St Moritz in 1928 and 1948.
77940.m: St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

77941.q: What do the best stand on at the award ceremony, as these pictures show?
77941.e: First, second and third places and a gold medal show the winners' podium. The winner stands in the middle on the highest step.
77941.m: On the winners' podium, the winner stands at the top.

77942.q: Which athletics event do these pictures show?
77942.e: A runner and several barriers stand for the hurdles. You have to jump over hurdles while running.
77942.m: In the hurdles, you jump over hurdles at full speed.

77943.q: Which athletics event do these pictures show?
77943.e: A long jump like a kangaroo's and a sandpit make long jump. After the run-up, you land in a pit of sand.
77943.m: In the long jump, you land in the sandpit.

77944.q: Which games do these pictures mean?
77944.e: A wheelchair and a medal in the stadium show the Paralympic Games. Athletes with disabilities compete there.
77944.m: At the Paralympics, people with disabilities compete.

77945.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77945.e: A curling stone, a brush and ice show curling. The players sweep in front of the stone so that it slides further.
77945.m: In curling, you sweep the ice in front of the stone.

77946.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77946.e: Sticks with a puck, ice and a goal show ice hockey. Each team has five outfield players and a goalkeeper on the ice.
77946.m: In ice hockey, you shoot the puck into the goal.

77947.q: Which winter sport do these pictures show?
77947.e: A sledge, the number four, ice and the chequered flag make the four-man bobsleigh. In St Moritz there is a bobsleigh run made of natural ice.
77947.m: Four people sit in a four-man bobsleigh.

77948.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77948.e: Snow and surfing make snowboarding, because you stand sideways on a board. Snowboarding has been an Olympic sport since 1998.
77948.m: In snowboarding, you stand sideways on a board.

77950.q: Which skiing event do these pictures show?
77950.e: A skier between lots of flags shows the slalom. You ski tightly around lots of gates.
77950.m: In the slalom, you ski around lots of tight gates.

77951.q: Which winter sport do these pictures mean?
77951.e: Dogs, a sledge and snow show sled dog racing. Huskies often pull the sledge.
77951.m: In sled dog racing, dogs pull the sledge.

77952.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77952.e: Ice, speed (lightning) and running make speed skating. You skate around a 400-metre track.
77952.m: In speed skating, only the time counts.

77953.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77953.e: A mouth and an organ make mouth organ, another name for the harmonica. You blow and suck air through small channels.
77953.m: You play the mouth organ with your mouth.

77954.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77954.e: A church and a keyboard show the church organ. It is played with hands and feet and has lots of pipes.
77954.m: You play the organ with your hands and feet.

77955.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77955.e: Bell (Glocke) and game (Spiel, the dice) make glockenspiel, a German word that is also used in English. You strike small metal bars with little mallets.
77955.m: On a glockenspiel, you strike metal bars.

77956.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77956.e: The stringed instrument with a round drum and the cowboy show the banjo. It is very popular in the folk music of the USA.
77956.m: The banjo has a round body like a drum.

77957.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77957.e: A stringed instrument and a very tall giraffe show the double bass. It is the largest and deepest stringed instrument in the orchestra.
77957.m: The double bass is the largest stringed instrument.

77958.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77958.e: A small guitar, flowers and an island show the ukulele. It comes from Hawaii and has four strings.
77958.m: The ukulele is a small guitar from Hawaii.

77959.q: Which instrument do these pictures make together?
77959.e: Electricity (lightning) and guitar make electric guitar. It needs an amplifier so that you can hear it loudly.
77959.m: The electric guitar needs an amplifier.

77960.q: Which Swiss folk instrument do these pictures show?
77960.e: A small accordion and the mountains show the Schwyzerörgeli. It is often played in Swiss folk music.
77960.m: The Schwyzerörgeli is a small accordion from Switzerland.

77961.q: Which instrument do these pictures mean?
77961.e: A kangaroo for Australia, wood and music show the didgeridoo. It is a long wind instrument of the Aborigines made from a hollow branch.

77962.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77962.e: A saxophone, a piano and a club at night go with jazz. Jazz began around 1900 in New Orleans and is all about improvising.

77963.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77963.e: A microphone, a cap and a speaking head show rap. In rap, you speak words rhythmically to the music.
77963.m: In rap, you speak words to a rhythm.

77964.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77964.e: A cowboy hat, a guitar and a horse go with country music. It comes from rural areas of the USA.
77964.m: Country music comes from the USA.

77965.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77965.e: A violin, a piano and an old clock go with classical music. Well-known composers are Mozart and Beethoven.
77965.m: Mozart and Beethoven wrote classical music.

77966.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77966.e: An island, music and the colours green, yellow and red show reggae. Reggae comes from Jamaica and became famous through Bob Marley.

77967.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77967.e: Blue, a guitar and a sad face show the blues. “To have the blues” means to be sad.

77968.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77968.e: A church, raised hands and music show gospel. Gospel songs are Christian songs from African American churches.
77968.m: Gospel is often sung by large choirs.

77969.q: Which style of music do these pictures mean?
77969.e: Heavy, metal and a guitar make heavy metal. Loud, distorted guitars are typical.
77969.m: Heavy metal is loud rock music with distorted guitars.

77970.q: Which famous ballet do these pictures show?
77970.e: Ballet shoes, a swan and water show “Swan Lake”. The music was written by Pyotr Tchaikovsky.
77970.m: The music for “Swan Lake” is by Tchaikovsky.

77971.q: Which Christmas ballet do these pictures show?
77971.e: A nut being cracked, ballet shoes and a Christmas tree show “The Nutcracker”. Tchaikovsky's ballet takes place on Christmas Eve.

77972.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77972.e: Carnival, drums, dancing and a beach go with the samba. It comes from Brazil and is danced at the carnival in Rio.

77973.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77973.e: Loud shoes to music show tap dance. The shoes have metal plates that click when you dance.
77973.m: In tap dance, metal plates on the shoes click.

77974.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77974.e: The number three, a dancing couple and violins show the waltz. It is danced in three-four time, especially in Vienna.
77974.m: The waltz is danced in three-four time.

77975.q: Which Italian folk dance do these pictures mean?
77975.e: A spider (tarantula) and dancing show the tarantella. According to an old legend, fast dancing was supposed to help against a tarantula bite.
77975.m: The tarantella is a fast dance from southern Italy.

77976.q: Which Spanish dance do these pictures mean?
77976.e: A ruffled dress, clapping, a guitar and a rose show flamenco. It comes from Andalusia in Spain.

77977.q: Which dance do these pictures mean?
77977.e: Acrobatics, spins, a cap and music show breakdance. It is part of hip-hop culture from New York.
77977.m: Breakdance is part of hip-hop culture.

77979.q: Which dice game do these pictures show?
77979.e: Snakes, ladders and a dice show snakes and ladders. You climb up the ladders and slide down the snakes.
77979.m: In snakes and ladders, you slide down the snakes.

77980.q: Which board game do these pictures mean?
77980.e: A pawn, a king and a horse show chess. The horse is called the knight, and you want to checkmate the king.
77980.m: In chess, you want to checkmate the king.

77983.q: Which Swiss card game do these pictures mean?
77983.e: Playing cards with roses, acorns, bells and shields show Jass. It is the best-known card game in Switzerland.
77983.m: Jass is the most popular card game in Switzerland.

77984.q: Which puzzle game do these pictures mean?
77984.e: A puzzle piece and a picture show the jigsaw puzzle. You put lots of small pieces together to make a whole picture.
77984.m: In a jigsaw puzzle, you put pieces together to make a picture.

77986.q: Which device do these pictures make together?
77986.e: Needle, thread and a machine make sewing machine. With it, you sew fabric much faster than by hand.
77986.m: With a sewing machine you sew faster than by hand.

77987.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77987.e: A fishing rod, a fish and a river show fishing. In Switzerland you usually need a licence for it.
77987.m: In Switzerland you usually need a licence to go fishing.

77988.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77988.e: A seedling, a potted plant and water show gardening. Plants need soil, light and water.
77988.m: In gardening, you look after plants.

77989.q: What are you building, as these pictures show?
77989.e: A bird, a house and a hammer make the birdhouse. In winter you can feed birds in it.
77989.m: You build a birdhouse for birds.

77990.q: Which hobby do these pictures show?
77990.e: Scissors, paper and coloured pencils show crafts. You cut, stick and paint.
77990.m: In crafts, you cut and stick.

77991.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77991.e: Climbing and wall make climbing wall. In climbing centres there are walls with colourful holds.
77991.m: On a climbing wall, you hold on to holds.

77992.q: Which leisure activity do these pictures show?
77992.e: A kite and wind show kite flying. In autumn it is often windy enough for it.
77992.m: You need wind to fly a kite.

77994.q: Which paper craft do these pictures mean?
77994.e: Paper, a bird and Japan show origami. In this Japanese art, you fold figures such as the crane out of paper.
77994.m: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

77995.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77995.e: Air (aeroplane) and port (anchor) make airport. The largest airport in Switzerland is in Zurich.
77995.m: The largest airport in Switzerland is near Zurich.

77996.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
77996.e: Train and ticket make train ticket. In Switzerland, people say “Billett” for a ticket.
77996.m: You need a ticket to travel by train.

77997.q: Which travel document do these pictures mean?
77997.e: Passport control, a red booklet and a suitcase show the passport. The Swiss passport is red.

77998.q: Which book do these pictures mean?
77998.e: Travel, a book and good tips make a travel guide. It describes the sights at a holiday destination.
77998.m: A travel guide gives tips for your destination.

77999.q: Which famous Swiss train do these pictures mean?
77999.e: A glacier, a train and mountains show the Glacier Express. It runs from Zermatt to St Moritz and is said to be the slowest express train in the world.
77999.m: The Glacier Express runs from Zermatt to St Moritz.

78000.q: What kind of journey do these pictures show?
78000.e: A big ship, the sea and islands show a cruise. You travel on a ship and visit several places.
78000.m: On a cruise, you live on a ship.

78001.q: Which travel problem do these pictures mean?
78001.e: Flying, a different time and tiredness show jet lag. It happens when you fly quickly across several time zones.
78001.m: Jet lag comes from flights across time zones.

78002.q: Which means of transport do these pictures make together?
78002.e: Cable, car and mountain make cable car. The cabin hangs from cables and travels up the mountain.
78002.m: On a cable car, the cabin hangs from cables.

78003.q: Which holiday activity do these pictures show?
78003.e: Hiking boots, a mountain and a map show hiking. Switzerland has a dense network of footpaths marked in yellow.
78003.m: Swiss footpaths are marked in yellow.

78004.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78004.e: Air and bed (mattress) make airbed. You can lie on it by the water or sleep on it in a tent.
78004.m: An airbed is filled with air.

78005.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78005.e: Sun and umbrella make sun umbrella. It gives shade on the beach or in the garden.

78006.q: What kind of holiday do these pictures show?
78006.e: A tent, a campfire and a forest show a camp. The Scouts, for example, often go to camp in summer.
78006.m: At camp, you sleep in a tent.

78008.q: Which feeling on holiday do these pictures mean?
78008.e: A house, a thought and sadness show homesickness. You miss your home, for example at camp.
78008.m: Homesickness means you miss your home.

78009.e: A postbox, a picture and the beach show the picture postcard. It shows a picture of the holiday place and is sent by post.
78009.m: People like to send a postcard from their holidays.

78010.q: Which holiday problem do these pictures mean?
78010.e: Lots of cars and a snail show the traffic jam. At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams in front of the Gotthard road tunnel.
78010.m: At the start of the holidays, there are often traffic jams at the Gotthard.

78011.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78011.e: A pumpkin, sweets and a ghost show Halloween. It is celebrated on 31 October.

78012.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78012.e: Masks, drums, trumpets and confetti show carnival (Fasnacht). The Basel carnival has been part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage since 2017.

78013.q: Which public holiday do these pictures mean?
78013.e: The numbers 1 and 8, fireworks and paper lanterns show Swiss National Day on 1 August. It is the national holiday of Switzerland.
78013.m: Switzerland's national holiday is on 1 August.

78014.q: Which Zurich festival do these pictures mean?
78014.e: A snowman in the fire, horses and six o'clock show Sechseläuten. At 6 p.m., the Böögg is set alight, and riders circle the fire.
78014.m: At Sechseläuten, the Böögg is burnt.

78015.q: Which market in Bern do these pictures mean?
78015.e: Onions, shopping and the bear for Bern show the Zibelemärit, the onion market. It takes place every year on the fourth Monday in November.
78015.m: The Zibelemärit is an onion market in Bern.

78016.q: Which Swiss custom do these pictures mean?
78016.e: Decorated cows with bells coming down the mountain show the Alpine descent. In autumn, the animals come back from the Alpine pastures to the valley.
78016.m: In the Alpine descent, the cows return to the valley in autumn.

78017.q: Who comes on 6 December with these pictures?
78017.e: A man with a beard, mandarins and nuts show the Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas. He comes on 6 December, often together with Schmutzli.

78018.q: Which festival do these pictures mean?
78018.e: A big wheel, a merry-go-round and sweets show the Chilbi. That is what a funfair is called in Switzerland.
78018.m: A Chilbi is a funfair with rides.

78019.q: Which time of the church year do these pictures mean?
78019.e: Fir branches, candles and the number four show Advent. The Advent wreath has four candles for the four Sundays before Christmas.
78019.m: Four candles burn on the Advent wreath.

78021.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78021.e: Hearing (ear) and book make audiobook. A book is read aloud and you listen.
78021.m: You listen to an audiobook instead of reading it.

78022.q: Which place do these pictures mean?
78022.e: A clapperboard, popcorn and a ticket show the cinema. There you watch films on a big screen.
78022.m: At the cinema, you watch films on a screen.

78023.q: What kind of photo do these pictures mean?
78023.e: If you point your mobile at yourself, you take a selfie. A selfie is a photo you take of yourself.
78023.m: A selfie is a photo of yourself.

78024.q: Which word do these pictures make together?
78024.e: Computer and game (controller) make computer game. With games, you should pay attention to the recommended age.
78024.m: With computer games, you check the age rating.

78025.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78025.e: A pencil, a film strip and a mouse show the cartoon. Lots of drawn pictures are shown quickly one after another.
78025.m: A cartoon is made of lots of drawn pictures.

78026.q: What kind of film do these pictures mean?
78026.e: No sound, a film strip and a hat like Charlie Chaplin's show the silent film. Until the end of the 1920s, films mostly had no spoken sound.
78026.m: Silent films have no spoken sound.

78027.q: Which programme do these pictures mean?
78027.e: Sun and clouds, a television and a map show the weather forecast. It predicts the weather for the next few days.
78027.m: The weather forecast predicts the weather.

78098.q: Which saying with a colour does this picture puzzle show?
78098.e: Among several sheep, a black one stands out. “The black sheep” is someone who stands out in a group in a bad way.
78098.m: The black sheep of a family stands out because of bad behaviour.

78204.q: Which Bible story do these emojis show?
78204.e: A big ship, animals in pairs, rain, a dove and a rainbow: Noah saves his family and the animals from the Flood.
78204.m: After the Flood, Noah sent out a dove, which came back with an olive branch.

78346.q: Which animal behaviour do these pictures mean?
78346.e: In autumn, birds fly to warmer parts of the world. This behaviour is called bird migration; swallows from Switzerland, for example, spend the winter in Africa.
78346.m: Migratory birds spend the winter in warmer regions.

78393.e: A dinosaur in rock stands for a fossil. Fossils are the remains or traces of living things from earlier ages of the Earth, turned to stone.
78393.m: Fossils are evidence of life from prehistoric times.

78405.q: Which form of energy do these pictures mean?
78405.e: Wind turns a wheel, and this makes electricity. Wind turbines turn the movement energy of the air into electrical energy.
78405.m: Wind turbines use the movement energy of the air.

78428.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78428.e: The maple leaf is on Canada's flag, the beaver is an official national symbol and ice hockey is the national winter sport. Together, that makes Canada.
78428.m: Canada is the second largest country on Earth by area.

78429.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78429.e: Koalas live in the wild only in Australia, and almost all kangaroos live there too. The dry outback covers large parts of the country.
78429.m: Australia is both a country and a whole continent.

78430.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78430.e: Tacos, cacti and the colourful piñata are seen as typical of Mexico. Maize for tortillas was grown there thousands of years ago.
78430.m: Mexico is the Spanish-speaking country with the most people in the world.

78431.e: The picture shows Mount Fuji, the highest mountain in Japan, along with sushi and the Shinkansen high-speed train, which has been running since 1964.
78431.m: Mount Fuji is a volcano and, at 3776 metres, the highest mountain in Japan.

78432.q: Which country do these emojis show?
78432.e: The giant panda lives in the wild only in China; chopsticks and red lanterns, for example at the Lantern Festival, are part of Chinese culture.
78432.m: China is one of the countries with the most people on Earth.

78433.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78433.e: Elephants, curries and yoga, which has its origins in India, together point to India.

78434.q: Which country do these pictures mean?
78434.e: Camels in the desert, the pyramids and the crocodiles in the Nile point to Egypt.
78434.m: Egypt lies in north-east Africa on the Nile.

78437.q: Which city do these emojis mean?
78437.e: The bear is on the coat of arms of Bern, the Federal Palace is the seat of the Federal Council and Parliament, and in clear weather you can see the Alps. Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.
78437.m: Officially, Switzerland has no capital; Bern is the federal city.

78438.q: Which capital do these pictures show?
78438.e: The gate stands for the Brandenburg Gate, the bear for the city's coat of arms and the wall for the Berlin Wall, which divided the city from 1961 to 1989.
78438.m: The Wall divided Berlin into East and West for 28 years.

78440.q: Which capital do these emojis show?
78440.e: The stadium stands for the Colosseum, the fountain for the Trevi Fountain, pasta and scooters for Italian city life. Together that makes the Italian capital.
78440.m: The Colosseum is the largest amphitheatre of the ancient world.

78441.e: The guards outside Buckingham Palace, the red double-decker buses and the frequent rain are seen as typical of London.
78441.m: London lies on the Thames and is the capital of the United Kingdom.

78445.q: Which landmark do these emojis show?
78445.e: The statue holds a torch and a tablet with the date of the Declaration of Independence. France gave it to the USA, and it was unveiled in New York in 1886.
78445.m: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the USA.

78471.q: Which form of trade do these emojis show?
78471.e: The arrows in a circle show that a cow is swapped directly for grain, without any money at all.
78471.m: In barter, goods are swapped for each other without money.

78473.e: The goods leave your own country and go out into the world. Selling goods abroad is called exporting.
78473.m: Exports are goods that are sold abroad.

78511.e: The ticket divided by two makes half the price. With the Half Fare Travelcard, you travel on Swiss public transport at half price.
78511.m: With the Half Fare Travelcard, you pay only half price on public transport.

78515.e: Red plus sea makes the Red Sea between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, which is known for its colourful coral reefs and fish.
78515.m: The Red Sea is famous for its coral reefs.

78517.q: Which sea do these emojis show?
78517.e: Olives, lemons and lots of sun typically grow and thrive around the Mediterranean Sea, which separates Europe, Africa and Asia.
78517.m: Around the Mediterranean, there is a warm climate with dry summers.

78519.q: Which natural phenomenon do these emojis show?
78519.e: The pull of the Moon makes the sea level rise and fall regularly. This change between low tide and high tide is called the tides.
78519.m: Low and high tide are caused mainly by the pull of the Moon.

78520.q: Which climate zone do these emojis show?
78520.e: Palm trees, lots of rain and high temperatures all year round mark the tropics around the equator.
78520.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

78521.e: Penguins, snow and the polar night lasting for months mark the coldest areas of the Earth at the poles.
78521.m: In the polar zone, there is the polar night in winter.

78525.q: Which climate zone do these pictures mean?
78525.e: Autumn, spring, summer and winter show the four clear seasons. They mark the temperate zone, where Switzerland lies too.
78525.m: Switzerland lies in the temperate climate zone.

78527.q: Which vegetation zone do these emojis show?
78527.e: Sand, dromedaries, cacti and strong sun mark the desert. So little rain falls there that hardly any plants grow.
78527.m: Very little rain falls in the desert.

78573.q: Which technology do these emojis show?
78573.e: The computer receives a radio signal and needs no network cable. A wireless local network is called Wi-Fi or WLAN (Wireless Local Area Network).
78573.m: Wi-Fi connects devices to the network without cables.

78585.q: Which kind of picture do these emojis show?
78585.e: A painter looks in the mirror and paints himself. A picture like this is called a self-portrait; those by Rembrandt, for example, are famous.
78585.m: In a self-portrait, artists show themselves.

78588.q: Which art technique do these emojis mean?
78588.e: Lots of small coloured squares together make a picture. In a mosaic, you put small stones or pieces of glass together to make a picture.
78588.m: A mosaic is made of lots of small coloured stones.

78589.q: Which painting technique goes with these emojis?
78589.e: Painting is done on paper with water, a brush and paint. Painting with see-through water-based paints is called watercolour (in German “Aquarell”, from Latin aqua, water).
78589.m: A watercolour is painted with water-based paints.

78606.q: Which running event do these pictures mean?
78606.e: The number 42 stands for the distance of 42.195 kilometres. This long-distance race is called a marathon, named after the Greek town of Marathon.

78607.q: Which sport do these emojis show?
78607.e: Swimming, cycling and running are done straight after each other. This endurance sport is called triathlon (Greek tri, three).
78607.m: The triathlon is made up of swimming, cycling and running.

78609.e: A ball lies about 11 metres in front of the goal, and only the goalkeeper may try to stop it. This kick is called a penalty.
78609.m: A penalty is taken from the penalty spot.

78622.q: Which job with a French name goes with these emojis?
78622.e: A person with a cap drives other people in a car. Someone who drives a vehicle as a job is called a chauffeur.
78622.m: A chauffeur drives other people in a car.

78623.q: Which job with a French name is meant?
78623.e: Hair is cut with scissors, and the striped sign stands for a salon. In Switzerland, a hairdresser is called a coiffeur.
78623.m: The coiffeur cuts and styles hair.

78631.q: Which painting do these emojis mean?
78631.e: Leonardo da Vinci painted the woman with the mysterious smile in front of a wide landscape; the picture hangs today in the Louvre in Paris.
78631.m: The Mona Lisa's smile is seen as the most famous in the history of art.

78764.q: Which term from psychology do these pictures mean?
78764.e: Sun and a thought bubble with a sleepy face make day and dream. In a daydream, your thoughts wander while you are awake.
78764.m: In a daydream, your thoughts wander even though you are awake.

78778.q: Which term from the digital world do these pictures mean?
78778.e: A screen (mobile and computer) is photographed. A photo of the screen is called a screenshot.
78778.m: With a screenshot, you save a picture of the screen.

78790.q: Which term from linguistics do these pictures mean?
78790.e: Hands and hand signs replace the spoken word. Deaf people communicate with sign language; in Switzerland there are three sign languages.
78790.m: Sign languages are full languages that work with the hands, the face and the body.

78919.q: What does a trimmed hornbeam hedge often do in winter?
78919.e: Many hornbeam hedges only lose their brown leaves in spring. So they stay thick even in winter.
78919.m: Hornbeam hedges often keep their dry leaves in winter.

78920.q: How many needles grow together from one spot on a Swiss stone pine?
78920.e: On the Swiss stone pine, five needles always grow in one bundle. That makes it easy to recognise.
78920.m: The Swiss stone pine has its needles in fives.

78921.q: What is inside the cones of the Swiss stone pine?
78921.e: Swiss stone pine cones contain nourishing seeds. They are called pine nuts, and you can eat them.
78921.m: Swiss stone pine cones contain edible little nuts.

78922.q: Which bird hides the nuts of the Swiss stone pine and so helps new trees to grow?
78922.e: In autumn the spotted nutcracker hides lots of pine nuts in the ground. Young trees grow from the stores it forgets.
78922.m: The spotted nutcracker plants Swiss stone pines.

78923.q: How old can a Swiss stone pine get?
78923.e: The Swiss stone pine grows slowly and can live a very long time. Some trees are several hundred to about 1000 years old.
78923.m: Swiss stone pines can get very old.

78924.q: What is the wood of the Swiss stone pine especially known for?
78924.e: Swiss stone pine wood smells nice and keeps its scent for a long time. People even fill pillows with its shavings.
78924.m: Swiss stone pine wood smells lovely.

78925.q: What can the Swiss stone pine cope with especially well?
78925.e: The Swiss stone pine grows where winters are very long and cold. It copes well with severe cold.
78925.m: The Swiss stone pine can stand severe cold.

a: a room panelled with Swiss stone pine
78926.e: In an Arvenstube the walls and ceiling are covered with Swiss stone pine wood. Rooms like this are common in houses in the Grisons.
78926.m: An Arvenstube is panelled with Swiss stone pine wood.

78927.q: What is another name for the Swiss stone pine?
78927.e: The Swiss stone pine is also called the arolla pine. In Switzerland people mostly call it “Arve”.
78927.m: The Swiss stone pine is also called the arolla pine.

79028.q: Which organ in your head do you think with?
79028.e: The brain is in the head. We use it to think, learn and remember.

79029.q: How many eyes does a person have?
79029.e: A person has two eyes. With two eyes you can judge well how far away something is.

79030.q: What is the front part of the head with the eyes, nose and mouth called?
79030.e: The eyes, nose and mouth are at the front of the head. This part is called the face.
79030.m: The eyes, nose and mouth are part of the face.

79031.q: Where on the body are the ears?
a: On the sides of the head
At the front of the neck
At the back of the neck
79031.e: The ears sit on the left and right of the head. That way we can hear which direction a sound comes from.
79031.m: The ears sit on the sides of the head.

79032.q: What grows on top of most people's heads?
79032.e: Hair grows on the head. It protects a little against sun and cold.

79033.q: What is the back of the neck called?
79033.e: At the back of the neck is the nape. Strong muscles there hold up the head.
79033.m: The back of the neck is called the nape.

79034.q: What do you wear round your neck in winter against the cold?
79034.e: A scarf keeps your neck warm. You wrap it round once or twice.
79034.m: A scarf keeps your neck warm.

79035.q: Which organ in your neck do you need for speaking and singing?
79035.e: The vocal cords sit in the voice box. When air flows past them, they vibrate and make sounds.
79035.m: The voice box makes our voice.

79036.q: Which piece of jewellery do you wear round your neck?
79036.e: You put a necklace round your neck. Often a small pendant hangs from it.
79036.m: You wear a necklace round your neck.

a: Between the neck and the arm
Between the knee and the foot
Between the hand and the finger
Between the tummy and the leg
79037.e: The shoulder is at the top side of the trunk. That is where the arm begins.
79037.m: The shoulder is between the neck and the arm.

79038.q: What is the flat bone at the back of the shoulder called?
79038.e: The shoulder blade is a flat, triangular bone. It is at the back of the upper back.
79038.m: The shoulder blade is at the back of the shoulder.

79039.q: Which joint can you move furthest in a circle?
79039.e: The shoulder joint is the most movable joint in the body. That is why you can swing your arm in a big circle.
79039.m: The shoulder is our most movable joint.

79040.q: What do you often show when you shrug your shoulders?
a: That you do not know something
79040.e: When you shrug, you lift your shoulders briefly. That way you show without words: I don't know.
79040.m: A shrug often means “I don't know”.

79041.q: Which part of the arm is directly below the shoulder?
79041.e: The upper arm reaches from the shoulder to the elbow. There is a long bone inside it.
79041.m: The upper arm begins below the shoulder.

79042.q: What does it mean to “give someone the cold shoulder”?
a: To give them a friendly hug
79042.e: The saying means that you deliberately ignore someone. You turn away from them, so to speak.
79042.m: If you give someone the cold shoulder, you ignore them.

79043.q: In which sport do players wear big shoulder pads?
79043.e: In ice hockey, players often crash into each other. Shoulder pads under the shirt cushion the knocks.
79043.m: Ice hockey players protect their shoulders with pads.

79044.q: Which joint is in the middle of the arm?
79044.e: The elbow is roughly in the middle of the arm. That is where you can bend the arm.
79044.m: The elbow is in the middle of the arm.

79045.q: What can you do with your elbow?
79045.e: With the elbow joint you bend your arm and straighten it again. That way you can, for example, bring a spoon to your mouth.
79045.m: We bend our arm with the elbow.

79047.q: What was the “ell” used for in the past?
79047.e: The ell used to be a measure of length. It was roughly the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger.
79047.m: The ell used to be a measure of length.

79048.q: Where is the “funny bone” that tingles so much when you knock it?
79048.e: At the elbow, a nerve lies just under the skin. If you knock it there, it tingles all the way into your fingers.
79048.m: The funny bone is at the elbow.

79049.q: Roughly how does the elbow move when you bend it?
79049.e: The elbow folds the arm mainly in one direction, like a door on its hinge. In addition, the forearm can twist.
79049.m: The elbow folds like a hinge.

79050.q: What does it mean to “elbow your way” forward?
a: To push ahead without caring about others
79050.e: If you elbow your way forward, you push in front and only think of yourself. It is a saying.
79050.m: If you elbow your way forward, you push ahead without caring about others.

79051.q: Which joint connects the hand to the forearm?
79051.e: The wrist is where the hand begins. It makes the hand movable.
79051.m: The wrist connects the hand and forearm.

79052.q: Where do you usually wear a wristwatch?
79052.e: A wristwatch goes round the wrist. That way you can check the time quickly.
79052.m: You wear a wristwatch on your wrist.

79053.q: How many wrist bones does one hand have?
79053.e: There are eight small wrist bones in the wrist. They are arranged in two rows.

79054.q: Which joint do people especially often injure when they fall onto an outstretched hand?
79054.e: When people fall, they often catch themselves with their hands. This puts a lot of strain on the wrist, and it can break.
79054.m: When you fall onto your hand, the wrist often suffers.

79055.q: Which part of the arm is between the wrist and the elbow?
79055.e: The forearm reaches from the wrist to the elbow. There are two bones inside it.
79055.m: The forearm is between the wrist and the elbow.

79056.q: What do you mainly move when you wave your hand?
79056.e: When you wave, your hand tips back and forth. The wrist makes this movement possible.
79056.m: When you wave, your wrist moves.

79057.q: Which is the largest joint in the human body?
79057.e: The knee joint is the largest human joint. It carries a lot of weight when you walk and jump.
79057.m: The knee is our largest joint.

79058.q: What do you wear on your knees for protection when inline skating?
79058.e: Knee pads have hard shells. They protect your knees if you fall.
79058.m: Knee pads protect your knees when skating.

79059.q: What is the soft area at the back of the knee called?
79059.e: At the back of the knee there is a small hollow. It is called the hollow of the knee.
79059.m: The hollow of the knee is at the back of the knee.

79060.q: How do many babies get about before they can walk?
a: They crawl on their hands and knees
79060.e: Many babies crawl first. They support themselves on their hands and knees.
79060.m: Babies crawl on their hands and knees.

a: At the back of the foot
At the front by the toes
At the top of the knee
At the bottom of the hand
79061.e: The heel is the round back part of the foot. A lot of weight rests on it.
79061.m: The heel is at the back of the foot.

79062.q: What is the largest bone in the foot called?
79062.e: The heel bone is the largest bone of the foot. It forms the heel.
79062.m: The heel bone is the largest foot bone.

79063.q: Which part of the foot usually touches the ground first when you walk normally?
79063.e: When you walk, you usually put your foot down heel first. Then it rolls forwards.
79063.m: When you walk, the heel touches down first.

79064.q: Where do you often get a blister in new, stiff shoes?
79064.e: New shoes often rub at the back of the heel. The rubbing causes a blister.
79064.m: New shoes often rub on the heel.

79065.q: What is the raised part of the shoe under the heel called?
79065.e: The heel of a shoe is the raised back part of the sole. It sits exactly under your heel.
79065.m: The shoe's heel sits under your heel.

79066.q: What does it mean to be “hot on someone's heels”?
79066.e: If you are hot on someone's heels, you follow them very closely. The saying fits, for example, a chase.
79066.m: If you are on someone's heels, you follow them closely.

79067.q: What forms on your heels if you often go barefoot?
79067.e: The skin on the heel gets thicker and harder from pressure. This hard layer is called hard skin.
79067.m: Hard skin forms on your heels.

79068.q: How many toes does a person have altogether on both feet?
79068.e: Each foot has five toes. Together that makes ten toes.

79069.q: What is the thickest toe on the foot called?
79069.e: The big toe is the thickest and strongest. When you walk, you push off with it.
79069.m: The big toe is the thickest.

79070.e: Right on the outside of the foot is the little toe. It is easy to stub on table legs.
79070.m: The smallest toe is right on the outside.

79071.q: How is it best to cut toenails?
79071.e: Toenails cut straight across are less likely to grow into the skin. That prevents pain.

79072.q: What do your toes especially help you with?
79072.e: When you stand and walk, your toes press against the ground. That way they help you not to fall over.

79073.q: In which dance do dancers in pointe shoes stand on the tips of their toes?
79073.e: In ballet there is pointe work. The dancers stand on the tips of their toes in special shoes.
79073.m: In ballet you dance on the tips of your toes.

79074.q: How many toes does a chicken usually have on one foot?
79074.e: Most chickens have four toes on each foot. A few breeds have five.
79074.m: A chicken usually has four toes on each foot.

a: At the front in the middle of the tummy
79075.e: The belly button is on the front of the tummy, roughly in the middle. Almost everyone has one.
79075.m: The belly button is on the front of the tummy.

79076.q: What actually is the belly button?
79076.e: The belly button is a scar that everyone gets as a baby. After that it stays for life.
79076.m: The belly button is a scar.

79077.q: What sometimes collects in the belly button?
79077.e: Fine fibres come off clothes. They can collect in the belly button as fluff.
79077.m: Fluff sometimes collects in the belly button.

79078.q: Which of these animals also has a navel?
79078.e: Mammals such as dogs have a navel, often well hidden under their fur. Chickens, frogs and fish hatch from eggs and do not have a navel like this.
79078.m: Mammals such as dogs have a navel too.

79079.q: How is it best to clean your belly button?
a: Gently with water in the shower
79079.e: In the shower you can wash your belly button gently with water and a little soap. Then dry it well.
79079.m: You wash your belly button gently in the shower.

79080.q: What do people mean when they say a place is “the navel of the world”?
a: It is the most important centre
79080.e: The navel is in the middle of the tummy. That is why a particularly important place is also called “the navel of the world”.

79081.q: Which long organ lies in many loops behind the belly button?
79081.e: The gut lies in the tummy in many coils. It digests the food further.
79081.m: The gut lies behind the belly button.

79082.q: Which part of the body is at the front between the belly button and the neck?
79082.e: Above the tummy comes the chest and then the neck. The heart and lungs are in the chest.
79082.m: The chest is above the tummy.

79083.q: What is the chain of bones in the middle of the back called?
79083.e: The spine runs from the head to the pelvis. It keeps the body upright.
79083.m: The spine is in the middle of the back.

79084.q: What is the right way to carry your school bag?
79084.e: With both straps, the weight is spread evenly. That is kind to your back.
79084.m: You carry your school bag on both shoulders.

79085.q: Which of these animals has a spine like us?
79085.e: Fish are vertebrates like us and have a spine. Snails, worms and insects do not have one.

79086.q: Which swimming stroke is swum on your back?
79086.e: In backstroke you lie in the water with your face upwards. You look up at the sky.
79086.m: In backstroke you lie on your back.

79087.q: Which animal carries a hard shell on its back?
79087.e: The tortoise has a firm shell on its back. When there is danger, it pulls in its head and legs.

79088.q: What is good for a healthy back?
79088.e: Exercise strengthens the muscles of the back. Strong muscles support the spine.

a: At the back of the head
79089.e: The forehead is the top part of the face. It reaches from the eyebrows up to the hairline.
79089.m: The forehead is above the eyes.

79090.q: What is between the forehead and the eyes?
79090.e: The eyebrows grow below the forehead. They keep sweat away from the eyes.
79090.m: The eyebrows are below the forehead.

79091.q: What do you often show when you frown?
a: That you are thinking or annoyed
79091.e: When you frown, wrinkles form on your forehead. Often you are thinking hard or are unhappy.

79092.q: Where can you take a temperature with a special thermometer without using the mouth?
79092.e: There are forehead thermometers. You hold them against or in front of the forehead and read off the temperature.
79092.m: You can also take a temperature on the forehead.

79093.q: What do you wear round your forehead during sport so that no sweat runs into your eyes?
79093.e: A headband soaks up sweat. That way you can see clearly during sport.
79093.m: A headband keeps sweat away from your eyes.

79094.q: What is the bone under the forehead called?
79094.e: The skull is made of several bones. At the top front is the frontal bone.
79094.m: The frontal bone is under the forehead.

79095.q: What does the German saying “jemandem die Stirn bieten” (literally ‘to offer someone your forehead’) mean?
a: To stand up to them bravely
To agree with them straight away
To greet them in a friendly way
79095.e: If you “offer someone your forehead”, you face up to them bravely. You do not simply give in.
79095.m: This German saying means to stand up to someone bravely.

79096.q: Which mythical animal has a horn in the middle of its forehead?
79096.e: The unicorn is a mythical creature from legends. It looks like a horse with a horn on its forehead.
79096.m: The unicorn has a horn on its forehead.

79097.q: What do people often put on the forehead to cool it when someone has a fever?
79097.e: A damp, cool flannel on the forehead feels nice when you have a fever. It cools the skin a little.
79097.m: With a fever, a cool flannel on the forehead feels good.

a: At the bottom of the face under the mouth
79098.e: The chin is the lowest part of the face. It is directly below the mouth.
79098.m: The chin is below the mouth.

79099.q: What does Samichlaus (Swiss St Nicholas) have on his chin and cheeks?
79099.e: In Switzerland, Samichlaus comes on 6 December. He has a long white beard.

79100.q: Which instrument do you hold between your chin and shoulder?
79100.e: When you play the violin, it rests on your shoulder. Your chin holds it in place.
79100.m: You hold the violin in place with your chin.

79101.q: What do we humans have that even chimpanzees lack?
79101.e: Humans are the only living things with a real chin that sticks out. Apes do not have one either.
79101.m: Only humans have a real chin.

79102.q: Where are you looking when you put your chin on your chest?
79102.e: When your chin goes to your chest, your head tips forwards. Then you look down.
79102.m: With your chin on your chest, you look down.

79103.q: What is the area on the side of the head between the eye and the ear called?
79103.e: The temple is on the left and right of the head, next to the eye. The skull is a little thinner there.
79103.m: The temple is between the eye and the ear.

79104.q: Which bird can turn its head especially far round?
79104.e: Owls can turn their head very far, up to three quarters of a full circle. That is because their eyes can hardly move.
79104.m: The owl turns its head very far.

79105.q: What does it mean to “bury your head in the sand”?
a: To refuse to see a problem
79105.e: The saying describes someone who closes their eyes to a problem. They hope it will go away by itself.
79105.m: If you bury your head in the sand, you refuse to see a problem.

79106.q: What do you often have with a cold when swallowing hurts?
79106.e: With a cold, the inside of the throat can be inflamed. Then swallowing hurts.
79106.m: With a cold you often have a sore throat.

79107.q: What does the German saying “Hals über Kopf” (literally ‘neck over head’) mean?
a: In a great rush, without thinking
79107.e: If you do something “neck over head”, you act in a great hurry. You hardly think about it.
79107.m: “Hals über Kopf” means in a great rush.

79108.q: According to an old table rule, what should you not put on the table when eating?
79108.e: A well-known table rule says: elbows do not belong on the table when eating. Your hands may rest on the table.
79108.m: Elbows do not belong on the table when eating.

79109.q: In which animal is a joint on the front leg called the “knee”, although it is really like our wrist?
79109.e: The so-called knee on a horse's front leg matches our wrist. The horse's real knee is much higher up on the back leg.
79109.m: A horse's front “knee” is really a wrist.

79110.q: In which direction can you bend your lower leg at the knee?
79110.e: The knee joint bends the lower leg backwards. Forwards it can only be straightened.
79110.m: The knee bends the leg backwards.

79111.q: Where do children often graze their skin when they fall over in the playground?
79111.e: If you fall forwards, you often land on your knees. The skin easily gets grazed.
79111.m: When you fall over, you often graze your knees.

79112.q: Which part of the leg is above the knee?
79112.e: The thigh is between the hip and the knee. There is a long, strong bone inside it.
79112.m: The thigh is above the knee.

79113.q: What does the German saying “etwas auf die leichte Schulter nehmen” (literally ‘to take something on the light shoulder’) mean?
a: To be able to carry it easily
79113.e: If you take something “on the light shoulder”, you think it is unimportant. Often it turns out to be more important than you thought.
79113.m: This German saying means not taking something seriously.

79114.q: What does it mean to “have someone's back”?
79114.e: If you have someone's back, you help them and stand by them. That makes the other person feel safer.
79114.m: If you have someone's back, you support them.

79115.q: Which wild animal of the Swiss Alps has a beard on its chin when it is male?
79115.e: The male ibex has a short beard under its chin. It also has large, curved horns.
79115.m: The ibex has a beard on its chin.

79116.q: What do many people rest their chin on when they sit thinking at a table?
79116.e: When thinking, many people rest their chin in their hand. That way the head rests comfortably.
79116.m: When thinking, people often rest their chin in their hand.

79117.q: What do many grown men remove from their chin and cheeks with a razor in the morning?
79117.e: In many men, short beard hairs grow every day. If they do not want a beard, they shave them off.

79118.q: Where do many people at the swimming pool wear the key for their locker?
79118.e: The locker key often hangs on a rubber band. You slip it over your wrist and so have the key with you while you swim.
79118.m: At the swimming pool you wear the key on your wrist.

79119.q: What is the part of a shirt that goes round the neck called?
79119.e: The collar is the top edge of the shirt. It goes all the way round the neck.
79119.m: The collar goes round the neck.

79120.q: What are you doing when you “crane your neck”?
79120.e: If you crane your neck, you stretch your head and neck upwards. That way you can see over other people.
79120.m: If you crane your neck, you want to see something.

79121.q: Which bird has only two toes on each foot?
79121.e: The ostrich is the only bird with only two toes on each foot. This helps it run fast.
79121.m: The ostrich has two toes on each foot.

79122.q: What do you sit on in the heel sit position?
79122.e: In the heel sit you kneel and sit with your bottom on your heels. You may know this position from PE.
79122.m: In the heel sit you sit on your heels.

79123.q: Where do koala mothers carry their older young around?
79123.e: When the koala joey is bigger, it clings to its mother's fur. It then rides along on her back.
79123.m: Koala joeys ride on their mother's back.

79124.q: What does it mean to talk about someone “behind their back”?
79124.e: If you talk behind someone's back, you talk about a person who is not there. The other person does not notice.
79124.m: Talking behind someone's back means talking secretly.

79125.q: What does it mean to “rack your brains”?
a: To think hard about something for a long time
79125.e: The saying describes someone who thinks for a long time about a difficult question. Of course, nothing actually gets damaged.
79125.m: If you rack your brains, you think for a long time.

79126.q: How does your chin move when you nod your head to say “yes”?
79126.e: When you nod, you lower and raise your head. Your chin moves up and down.
79126.m: When you nod, your chin moves up and down.

79127.q: What do people often wrap round a sprained wrist?
79127.e: An elastic bandage supports the injured joint. It also helps it to swell less.
79127.m: A sprained wrist is supported with a bandage.

79318.q: Why are pebbles from a stream usually round and smooth?
a: The water has rolled them for a long time
79318.e: The water rolls the stones back and forth in the stream for a long time. This wears the corners away, and the stones become round and smooth.
79318.m: Pebbles are worn round by the water.

79319.q: Where can you find lots of pebbles?
a: On the bank of a river
79319.e: Rivers and streams carry stones along and leave them on the bank. That is why there are lots of pebbles there.
79319.m: There are lots of pebbles on a riverbank.

79320.q: What do you call throwing flat stones across a lake so that they bounce several times?
79320.e: If you throw a flat pebble low across the water, it bounces several times. Some people also call it skipping stones.
79320.m: A flat pebble can bounce across the water.

79321.q: Which shape is best for making a stone bounce across the water?
79321.e: A flat, round stone glides well over the surface of the water. That is why it bounces more often than a ball-shaped stone.
79321.m: Flat, round stones bounce best across the water.

79322.q: Where do the pebbles in Swiss rivers originally come from?
79322.e: In the mountains, stones break off rocks. Streams and rivers carry them down the valley, and on the way they become round.
79322.m: Many pebbles originally come from the mountains.

79323.q: What do you call lots of small pebbles together, for example on a garden path?
79323.e: Gravel is made of lots of small, roundish stones. It is used for paths, squares and in building.
79323.m: Gravel is made of lots of small stones.

79324.q: What is the rock on the Rigi called, in which lots of round pebbles are baked together?
79324.e: Nagelfluh is made of many round pebbles that are firmly cemented together. You can find it on the Rigi and the Rossberg, for example.
79324.m: Nagelfluh is full of round pebbles.

79325.q: Why do pebbles often look shinier when they are wet?
a: The water makes the colours glow
Wet stones are made of glass
79325.e: A thin layer of water makes the surface smooth. This lets you see the colours and patterns of the stones better.
79325.m: Wet pebbles show their colours better.

79326.q: What does granite usually look like?
79326.e: Granite is made of many small grains in different colours. That is why it looks speckled.

79327.q: Is granite a hard or a soft stone?
a: A stone as soft as chalk
79327.e: Granite is very hard and tough. That is why it is used for stairs, fountains and kitchen worktops.
79327.m: Granite is a very hard stone.

a: From hot, liquid rock deep inside the Earth
From sand pressed together on the beach
79328.e: Granite was formed from red-hot, liquid rock. It cooled slowly deep inside the Earth and became hard.
79328.m: Granite formed from liquid rock that cooled down.

79329.q: What often glitters in a piece of granite?
79329.e: Granite contains mica. These are thin flakes that glitter in the light.

79330.q: What is granite often used for?
79330.e: Granite is hard and hardly wears away. That is why streets and squares are paved with it.
79330.m: Paving stones are made from granite.

79331.q: In which part of Switzerland is there a lot of granite?
79331.e: In the Alps, for example at the Grimsel and the Gotthard, there is a lot of granite. You can see huge grey rock faces there.
79331.m: There is a lot of granite in the Swiss Alps.

79332.q: What is the most common colour of granite?
79332.e: Many granites are grey with light and dark dots. But there is also reddish granite.

79333.q: What does the German saying “auf Granit beissen” (to bite on granite) mean?
79333.e: Granite is so hard that you cannot bite into it. If you “bite on granite”, you do not get what you want, a bit like hitting a brick wall.
79333.m: If you bite on granite, you get nowhere.

79334.q: What did a lot of limestone form from?
a: From the shells of sea creatures
79334.e: Long ago, many animals with shells lived in the sea. Their shells sank to the seabed and turned into limestone.
79334.m: A lot of limestone formed from the shells of sea creatures.

79335.q: Which mountain range in north-west Switzerland is largely made of limestone?
79335.e: The Jura is a mountain range made of limestone. You often find fossilised shells from an ancient sea in it.
79335.m: The Jura is largely made of limestone.

79336.q: What happens if you drip vinegar onto limestone?
79336.e: Vinegar is an acid. It dissolves limestone, and this makes tiny bubbles that foam.

79337.q: What are caves with spikes of limestone hanging from the ceiling called?
79337.e: Water dissolves limestone and drips from the cave ceiling. It leaves limestone behind, and slowly dripstones grow.
79337.m: Spikes of limestone grow in dripstone caves.

79338.q: What kind of stone is natural chalk?
79338.e: Natural chalk is a soft, white limestone. It is made of tiny shells of sea creatures.
79338.m: Natural chalk is a soft limestone.

79339.e: Limestone is usually light coloured, often grey, whitish or yellowish. That is why limestone cliffs shine brightly in the sun.

79340.q: What is the huge cave in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz called?
79340.e: The Hölloch is in the Muota valley in the canton of Schwyz. It is one of the longest caves in the world and lies in limestone.
79340.m: The Hölloch is a huge cave in limestone.

79341.q: Which white coating builds up inside a kettle over time?
79341.e: Tap water contains dissolved lime. When the water boils, it is left behind as a white coating in the kettle.
79341.m: Limescale builds up in a kettle over time.

79342.q: What are the limestone spikes called that grow down from the ceiling of a cave?
79342.e: Stalactites hang down from the ceiling. The dripstones that grow up from the floor are called stalagmites.
79342.m: Stalactites hang from the cave ceiling.

79343.e: Sandstone is made of lots of grains of sand. Over a long time they were pressed and cemented together.
79343.m: Sandstone is made of grains of sand stuck together.

79344.q: Which stone is much of Bern's old town built from?
79344.e: Many houses, the arcades and the Minster in Bern are built of sandstone. Bernese sandstone is greenish grey.
79344.m: Bern's old town is built of sandstone.

79345.q: What happens if you rub your finger hard over old sandstone?
79345.e: Sandstone is not as solid as granite. If you rub it, single grains of sand often come loose.
79345.m: Grains of sand come off sandstone easily.

79346.q: Why did sculptors like working with sandstone?
79346.e: Sandstone is softer than many other stones. That is why it can easily be shaped with a chisel and hammer.

79347.q: Which famous red rock in Australia is made of sandstone?
79347.e: Uluru is a huge rock in the middle of Australia. It is made of sandstone and glows red at sunset.
79347.m: Uluru in Australia is made of sandstone.

79348.q: What wears sandstone down over time so that it crumbles?
79348.e: Rain, frost and wind gradually loosen grains from the sandstone. That is why old sandstone buildings often need repairing.
79348.m: Wind and rain make sandstone crumble.

79349.e: Depending on what is between the grains of sand, sandstone can be yellow, red, brown or grey. Red sandstone contains iron, for example.

79350.q: What did sandstone form from a very long time ago?
a: From sand on beaches, in rivers or deserts
79350.e: Sand settled in thick layers on beaches, in rivers or in deserts. Under pressure it slowly turned into solid stone.
79350.m: Sandstone formed from layers of sand.

79351.q: Which stone did marble form from?
79351.e: Marble forms when limestone deep inside the Earth is strongly heated and squeezed. This changes the stone.

79352.q: What is white marble especially famous for?
79352.e: White marble can be carved finely and has a lovely shine. That is why artists have made famous statues from it.
79352.m: Statues are made from white marble.

79353.q: Which country does the famous Carrara marble come from?
79353.e: Carrara is a town in Italy. White marble has been quarried there for over 2000 years.

79354.q: What stone is Michelangelo's famous statue “David” made of?
79354.e: Michelangelo carved “David” from a large block of white marble. The statue stands in Florence.

79355.q: Which famous building in India is built of white marble?
79355.e: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a tomb covered in white marble. The other buildings are made of red or pink sandstone.
79355.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

79356.q: Which little toy balls get their name from marble?
79356.e: In the past, these little balls were often made of marble. That is why they are called marbles.
79356.m: Marbles get their name from marble.

79357.e: Polished marble has a very smooth surface. It feels cool even on warm days.
79357.m: Polished marble is smooth and cool.

79358.q: How can you often recognise marble?
a: By its holes like in cheese
79358.e: Many kinds of marble have fine, coloured lines. These lines are called veins.

79359.q: What does a rock crystal look like?
79359.e: A rock crystal is colourless and see-through. It looks like clear glass or ice.
79359.m: A rock crystal is clear like glass.

79360.q: How many sides does a rock crystal have all the way round?
79360.e: A rock crystal is a column with six side faces. At the top it comes to a point.
79360.m: A rock crystal has six sides.

79361.q: What are people called in Switzerland who search the mountains for crystals?
79361.e: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler. They climb around the Alps looking for crystals.
79361.m: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler.

79362.q: Where in Switzerland can you find rock crystals?
a: In fields on the Central Plateau
79362.e: Rock crystals are found mainly in the Alps. The areas around the Grimsel and the Gotthard are especially well known.
79362.m: Rock crystals are found in the Swiss Alps.

79363.q: What did people long ago think a rock crystal was?
79363.e: In the past, many people believed rock crystal was ice that never melts. The word crystal comes from the Greek word for ice.
79363.m: People used to think rock crystal was everlasting ice.

79364.q: Which mineral family does rock crystal belong to?
79364.e: Rock crystal is a very pure, clear form of quartz. Quartz is one of the most common minerals.

79365.q: What shape is the top end of a rock crystal?
79365.e: A rock crystal grows as a six-sided column. Its top end comes together in a point.
79365.m: A rock crystal has a point.

79366.e: Rock crystals grow in cracks and hollows in the rock. Over a long time, quartz from the water builds up there.
79366.m: Rock crystals grow in hollows in the rock.

79367.q: How long do large rock crystals take to grow?
79367.e: Rock crystals grow very slowly. Large crystals need a great many years.

79368.e: The ruby is a red gemstone. Its name comes from the Latin word for red.

79369.e: The emerald is a bright green gemstone. It is one of the most valuable gemstones.

79370.q: What colour is a sapphire usually?
79370.e: Most sapphires are blue. But there are also sapphires in other colours.

79371.e: The amethyst is a purple gemstone. It is a form of quartz.

79372.e: Gemstones are rare, beautiful and hard. That is why they are very precious.
79372.m: Gemstones are rare and therefore valuable.

79373.q: What do people do to gemstones to make them sparkle?
79373.e: Gemstones are cut into shape. Their many smooth faces make them sparkle in the light.

79374.q: What are gemstones often used for?
79374.e: Gemstones are beautiful and rare. That is why they are often set in rings, necklaces and crowns.
79374.m: Gemstones are often used for jewellery.

79375.q: Which of a queen's treasures is often set with lots of gemstones?
79375.e: The crowns of queens and kings are often decorated with gemstones. They show power and wealth.
79375.m: Crowns are often set with gemstones.

79376.q: Which stone is the hardest in nature?
79376.e: Diamond is the hardest natural material. It can scratch almost every other substance.
79376.m: Diamond is the hardest stone in nature.

79377.q: What is a diamond made of?
79377.e: A diamond is made only of carbon. That is the same substance that coal is mostly made of.
